passage: I'm Aditi, and on Saturday our school football team beat Ishita's team 2-1. I scored the winning goal. I felt like I was floating and wanted to shout it from the roof. But then I saw Ishita, their goalkeeper, sitting on the grass with her gloves in her lap. I remembered how it felt when we lost last year. So I hugged my teammates, thanked our defenders, and went over to say, "You saved so many shots, Ishita." She almost smiled. I'm still proud, but I'm glad I didn't do a victory dance in front of her.

qa.q: How did Aditi feel when she saw Ishita sitting on the grass?
qa.a: Aditi felt sympathy for Ishita, remembering how it felt to lose last year, so alongside her pride she wanted to be kind.

qa.q: What could Aditi do to keep that pride healthy?
qa.a: Keep thanking teammates and being kind to opponents, taking pride in the effort rather than showing off.

qa.q: How might Ishita have felt when Aditi praised her saves?
qa.a: Comforted a little, since she almost smiled, though she probably still felt sad about losing.

grounding: A child wins and feels wonderful, thanks the team and is kind to the losing goalkeeper instead of gloating.

passage:
At the village kho-kho tournament, Ritu's team won the final against Seema's team from the next village. Ritu felt like she was floating. She'd tagged three players in the last minute.
Her teammates lifted her on their shoulders. Some of them started chanting, "Losers, losers!" at Seema's team.
Ritu saw Seema sitting on the ground, face in her hands.
"Stop," Ritu said to her team. "We played well. That's enough."
She went over and held out her hand. "Seema, your team almost had us. Well played."
Seema looked up and shook it. Ritu turned back and thanked her own team, one by one.

qa.q: How many players did Ritu tag in the last minute?
How did Ritu feel after winning?
qa.a: She felt wonderful and proud, like she was floating.

qa.q: What did Ritu do that kept the win from becoming small?
qa.a: She stopped her team's chanting, congratulated Seema kindly, and thanked her own teammates.

qa.q: How might Seema have felt when Ritu's team chanted?
qa.a: Seema felt hurt and disappointed, sitting with her face in her hands.

grounding: A girl wins a match and feels proud; she stops her team's gloating, is kind to the losing captain and thanks her team.

passage:
At the swimming gala in Porto, Bao touched the wall first. He'd won the 50-metre freestyle! He pumped his fist and shouted. His coach grinned.
In the next lane, Ines was hanging onto the rope, breathing hard and looking at the scoreboard. She'd lost by a fingertip.
Bao's friend in the stands yelled, "Too slow, Ines!"
Bao shook his head at his friend. Then he swam over to Ines. "That was so close. You were really fast."
She nodded, still catching her breath. "Congrats."
Out of the pool, Bao thanked his coach and the relay team who'd cheered him on. He felt proud, but he also remembered how losing felt.

qa.q: How did Bao feel when he touched the wall first?
qa.a: He felt thrilled and proud, pumping his fist and shouting.

qa.q: What did Bao do that was kind to Ines?
qa.a: He stopped his friend's mocking and told Ines she was really fast.

qa.q: How might Ines feel after losing by a fingertip?
qa.a: Ines likely felt disappointed, but Bao's kindness may have made it easier.

grounding: A boy wins a race and feels proud; he stops his friend's mocking, is kind to the girl who lost and thanks his team.
